subject: Latency & throughput qualification — next steps and test matrix
messages:
From: Nelly Santos <nelly.santos@hypercloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Thanks for the demo this morning, Karthik — appreciate the quick walkthrough of Redwood's runtime and the live p95 numbers you showed. I wanted to confirm a couple of things before we kick off the lab: 

- We want a side-by-side run vs our hyperscaler provider (HyperCloud Managed Inference). Key metrics: p95 / p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state), and end-to-end cold-to-warm first-token time.
- Workload profile: 60% short prompts (~30 tokens), 30% mid (200 tokens), 10% long (1k tokens). Target concurrency ~120 concurrent requests to represent peak traffic.

We can share a sanitized sample corpus and can run the tests in our staging VPC (we'll provision a temporary endpoint). Question: do you need model binaries or just the model name and quantization profile? Also, we have a SOC2 evidence request — will need a short note about data handling during the lab (logs, retention).

Nelly
Ops — HyperCloud

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Nelly Santos <nelly.santos@hypercloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Hi Nelly — great to see alignment on metrics. Short answers up front: we only need the model name/version and a representative quantization profile; we can run our inference engine against the same model binary on your endpoint or spin an equivalent server in our lab depending on what you prefer. For SOC2, we'll send a short statement about ephemeral logs, no persistent storage of request payloads from labs, and access-limited artifact retention (logs removed after 30 days unless you request otherwise).

Proposed initial plan (high-level):
- Deliverables: p95/p99 latency tables, tokens/sec under sustained load, cold->warm TTF, and a side-by-side CSV and short PDF summary with charts.
- Test window: we can run initial A/Bs Thursday-Friday this week or early next week.
- Test matrix (draft): baseline HYPCLOUD-managed endpoint vs Redwood hosted endpoint variant and a Redwood-quantized variant. Variables: sequence length buckets, concurrency sweep (10/50/120/240), and batching on/off.

I looped in Marissa to own the lab orchestration and Sergio for the kernel/quantization knobs. Marissa — can you scope the test matrix and share a lab runbook? Sergio — we'll want to try an aggressive batch/kv-cache profile to show cost/throughput tradeoffs.

Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Nelly Santos <nelly.santos@hypercloud.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-06T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Thanks — drafting the lab runbook now. Attached: lab-test-matrix.csv (draft) and request package. High-level notes:

- Test matrix highlights (see attached CSV):
  * Models: "gptx-8b" (float16), "gptx-8b-4bit" (quantized), and your HyperCloud-managed endpoint using the same model.
  * Sequence buckets: short (<=32), mid (33-256), long (257-1024).
  * Concurrency sweep: 10, 50, 120, 240. We'll ramp and hold each step for 10 minutes to collect stable tokens/sec.
  * Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latencies, median and 95th tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and tail memory usage.
  * A/B design: parallel runs where possible; otherwise matched runs with identical payloads and randomized seeds.

- Logistics: please upload your sanitized sample payloads to the shared Drive link (https://drive.company/s/redwood-hypercloud-samples) and grant redwood-lab@redwood.ai read access. If you prefer we run in your staging VPC, please share an IAM temporary key and endpoint and we will execute from our test runner.

- Compliance note: we'll attach a one-page lab data handling statement. We do not persist raw prompts beyond the 30-day window for lab artifacts; aggregate metrics only for reports.

Attachments: lab-test-matrix.csv, redwood-lab-request-package.pdf

From: Nelly Santos <nelly.santos@hypercloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo follow-up

Appreciate the clear plan and the CSV draft. A few clarifying items before we schedule a hard run: 

1) Cold-to-warm: our current infra tends to show big variance — can you capture both first-token and first-50-tokens curves? That helps our SREs.
2) Model variants: we can provide the model binary (containerized) and our managed endpoint name. Please confirm you can pull the container from our ECR with a read-only role.
3) Cost-aware comparison: we want a delta sheet that maps tokens/sec to expected dollars at our current HyperCloud pricing and Redwood's hosted pricing — helps procurement.

If that all works, we'll upload sample payloads to the Drive and tag redwood-lab@redwood.ai with reader access by EOD. Also, do you have a short non-prod privacy addendum we can sign?

Best,
Nelly

Action items:
